First, we substitute $u={x}^{4}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4{x}^{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=4{x}^{3}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{4}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{8}+4}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{\infty }^{0}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}u=-{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{8}+4}\,\text{d}x & =-{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{u}{2})]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/7151efaca7e4356e590a437f5d50a2ab6e5646e960b7ffa82b0bbed27bb9db47.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{8}+4}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
